test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15th December 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Jagat Singh sold an article for Rs. 6,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs. 7,400, his profit would have been (2)/(3) of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell it to gain 25% profit?
solution:
**Given:**

First Selling Price = Rs.6,000 

Second Selling Price = Rs. 7,400 

Profit of second Selling Price = 2/3 of Loss of the first SP

**Formula used:**

CP = SP - Profit

CP = SP + Loss

Also, SP = CP x (100 + P)/100

**Calculation:**

Let Loss be 3x

⇒ Profit = 2x

Now, according to the statement

6000 + 3x = 7400 - 2x

⇒ x = 280

⇒ Profit = 2x = 560

⇒ CP = 7400 - 560 = 6840 

Now, SP for 25 % Profit = 6840 x (100 + 25)/100

⇒ SP = 8550

∴ To gain 25 % he should sell the article at 8550 Rs.

**∴ The option 1 is correct.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Let CP be x 

⇒ (x - 6000)/(7400 - x) = 3/2

⇒ x = 6840

Now, SP = 6840 (100 + 25) / 100 = 8550

**∴ Required SP is 8550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__** Profit is 2/3 of the Loss incurred not of the CP.
